subject: Status Update — Intermittent generation elongation impacting hosted inference (US-West)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: spike in generator tail latencies — US-West

Chloe —

Observability picked up a sustained p95/p99 elongation on generation API calls in the US-West cluster starting ~08:58 PST. Impact appears to be intermittent (short spikes) but elevated for the last ~12 mins. Affected surfaces: hosted text generation and chat routes (models: gpt-neo-7b-qa, opt-2.7b variants).

What we have so far:
- Traces show increased encoder->decoder handoff time on a subset of GPU hosts (host IDs included in attachment).
- No increased error rate (503s) observed — mostly longer tails and occasional token emission stalls.
- Autoscaling and routing are healthy; this looks like a per-host performance anomaly.

I attached a small snapshot of logs and trace ids (support_log_snapshot.txt). Asking ops to triage and looking for customer-facing comms to push to affected accounts.

Can you draft a short status note we can send to customers and post to statuspage? Ben/Laura looped for legal/CS copy-check.

—Dylan

Attachment: support_log_snapshot.txt (5 KB)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@novamedical.com>, ops@novamedical.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Status update — Intermittent generation elongation impacting hosted inference (US-West)

Ava / NovaMedical ops team —

I wanted to let you know we are investigating intermittent elongation (longer-than-expected generation times) affecting some hosted inference requests routed to our US-West region. Summary:

- Impact: elevated p95/p99 latency for text-generation and chat endpoints — in practice some requests are taking several extra seconds to stream the final tokens. There are no increased error responses (503/500) at the moment.
- Scope: a subset of traffic served from US-West; not all requests are affected.
- Start time: ~2025-08-16 08:58 PDT

What we're doing now:
- Ops has isolated the anomaly to a small set of GPU hosts and is redispatching traffic away from those hosts while we gather traces.
- Engineering is collecting harvest traces and runtime metrics to identify root cause; we have a Jira ticket open (JIRA-INFRA-1729).
- We will update the status page with incident details and any changes to customer impact.

Immediate guidance for NovaMedical:
- If you have critical time-sensitive calls, routing with a lower max_tokens per call (shorter expected outputs) will reduce exposure until we fully remediate.
- We are not recommending traffic throttling on your side at this time — we will advise if that changes.

Estimated next update: in 30–45 minutes or sooner if we have a mitigation. You can track live updates here: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-0816-gen-elongation

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency is material for your pipelines. Please reply here if you have any particular sessions or timestamps you want us to prioritize.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: harvest_trace-20250816.json (trace snapshot), support_log_snapshot.txt
From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@novamedical.com>

Subject: Re: Status update — Intermittent generation elongation impacting hosted inference (US-West)

Thanks Chloe — appreciate the quick heads up.

A couple quick questions:
- We had a batch job running at 09:05 PDT that reported timeouts for ~12% of calls; is that likely within the affected set?
- Is there a way for us to opt into a different region temporarily while you remediate, or will routing make that difficult?

If it helps, we can provide sample request ids from our side (we logged request ids and timestamps). Will send over a short list in a separate email.

—Ava

Ava —

Thanks, and yes please share the request ids/timestamps — that will help us narrow the traces for your batch job. Early triage shows those timeouts likely fall within the same affected timeframe, but we'll confirm after we examine your request ids.

Quick operational notes:
- Routing fallback is available; we can pin your account to US-East for a short window if you want us to do that immediately. If you want to proceed, tell me whether you want all traffic or only specific API keys moved.
- Ops has already redistributed traffic off 4 hosts and we saw an immediate drop in p95 for a slice of traffic; mitigation is in progress.

Statuspage and tracking: we posted the incident on the status page and opened a live incident (INC-2025-0816-GEN-ELONGATION). Engineering is tracking under JIRA-INFRA-1729. Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-0816-gen-elongation, JIRA-INFRA-1729.

I'll coordinate a follow-up once we confirm the targeted remediation is effective. If you want the temporary region switch, reply with preferred scope (all keys / key list) and I'll route the request to Ops for immediate action.

—Chloe
Account Executive, Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference
